details: Rising tensions between the US and Iran, including a tanker attack in the Strait of Hormuz and the US revocation of Iran's oil sales waiver, have increased geopolitical risks. This led to a sell-off in US equities, with the Nasdaq dropping over 1% and the S&P 500 falling 0.4%. The crypto market also retreated, with Bitcoin pulling back after failing to break above the $64,000 level, currently trading around $62,900.
title: Geopolitical Tensions Cause Market Pullback

details: The US economy added only 57,000 jobs in June, significantly missing the forecast of 110,000. This weak jobs report has increased expectations of the Federal Reserve cutting interest rates, as it reduces near-term pressure for rate increases. Following this, Bitcoin rebounded above $61,800, and Ethereum surged over 5%, with crypto market participants responding favorably to shifts in monetary policy expectations.
title: Soft US Jobs Data Fuels Fed Rate Cut Expectations, Bitcoin Rises

details: President Trump publicly reiterated his support for cryptocurrencies and suggested the potential launch of a US Treasury-linked digital asset account. This, combined with a broad rebound in US equities, further boosted crypto market sentiment. Bitcoin stabilized after a recent sale by Strategy and moved above the $64,000 level. Global regulatory adoption also continued, with Ripple securing a MiCA license in the EU and South Korea expanding virtual asset applications.
title: Trump's Crypto Support and US Digital Asset Hint Boost Market Sentiment

details: The US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) released its 2026 regulatory agenda, focusing on three key priorities: enabling compliant crypto product launches, establishing rules for crypto asset financing, and clarifying custody and on-chain trading frameworks for tokenized securities. This indicates a shift from an enforcement-driven model towards a clearer, rule-based framework for the industry.
title: SEC Shifts to Rule-Based Crypto Regulation

details: As of July 2026, the Federal Reserve is maintaining interest rates at elevated levels, signaling a "higher-for-longer" stance. The central bank remains cautious about inflationary pressures despite some signs of economic moderation, pushing back expectations for aggressive rate cuts that were anticipated earlier in the year. This stance contrasts with recent dovish comments from Fed Chair Warsh and weak jobs data, creating a complex outlook for markets.
title: Federal Reserve Sticks to "Higher-for-Longer" Rate Policy
